title: Non-forward simulation states are stationary
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $c$ be a configuration of the mapping machine on input $x$ whose state represents a simulated state of $M$. In non-forward mode, the configuration reached from $c$ after any natural number $t$ of steps is exactly $c$.
hypotheses_covered: M is a finite Boolean Turing machine
c is a mapping-machine configuration on input x
c is in a state representing a simulated state of M
